title: Giant-exchange-driven Vectorial Control of a Minimal Topological Magnet in Eu3In2As4
authors: Haonan Chen, Xunkai Duan, Guangyi Wang, Yuhan Du, Huayao Li, Jiayu Wang, Wenbin Wu, Zixuan Xu, Yingchao Xia, Jiaming Gu, Pengliang Leng, Lin Miao, Fengfeng Zhu, Xiang Yuan, Tong Zhou, Cheng Zhang
abstract: The interplay between magnetism and band topology provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its realization in materials is often constrained by weak exchange coupling and complex electronic structures. Here, a giant exchange coupling is identified in the newly predicted topological magnet Eu3In2As4, giving rise to magnetization-dependent band shifts of up to 300 meV. Together with its intrinsically soft magnetic response, this strong cou-pling enables systematic tuning of topological phases by both the magnitude and orientation of applied magnetic fields. The magneto-topological phase diagram is mapped out in which an antiferromagnetic topological insulator ground state evolves, under modest fields, into a pro-posed intermediate 2/3-ferrimagnetic phase, and further into fully polarized ferromagnetic states predicted to host either Weyl or nodal-ring semimetals. Notably, the Weyl phase corresponds to a minimal model hosting a single pair of Weyl nodes. Quantum oscillations, anomalous Hall transport and magneto-infrared spectroscopy consistently reveal exchange-driven band recon-struction across these transitions. Rotation of the magnetization theoretically provides an effi-cient means to tune the momentum-space positions and separations of the Weyl nodes. These results establish Eu3In2As4 as a model system for exploring how strong exchange coupling can be used to control topological band structures with minimal complexity.
summary: This work establishes $	ext{Eu}_3	ext{In}_2	ext{As}_4$ as a model system where strong exchange coupling allows systematic tuning of topological phases via external magnetic fields. By combining advanced magnetometry, spectroscopy, and transport measurements, the authors map out transitions from an antiferromagnetic insulator to ferromagnetic states hosting Weyl nodes. This demonstrates that magnetism can be used as a powerful knob to control electronic band topology in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The research aims to control quantum states of matter by integrating intrinsic magnetism with band topology, overcoming limitations posed by weak exchange coupling in existing materials.
main_result: The material $	ext{Eu}_3	ext{In}_2	ext{As}_4$ exhibits a predictable sequence of magnetic phase transitions (AFM $ightarrow 2/3$-FiMa $ightarrow$ FM) driven by external fields, leading to topological phases like Weyl semimetals.
method: The study combines theoretical calculations (DFT with SOC) predicting band structures for different magnetic states with multiple experimental probes including magneto-transport ($ho_{xx}$, AHE), magneto-infrared spectroscopy, and magnetization measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the topological magnet $	ext{Eu}_3	ext{In}_2	ext{As}_4$. The model relies on identifying a 'giant exchange coupling' that causes large, magnetization-dependent band shifts (up to 300 meV) across various magnetic phases.
key_observables: Magnetization $M(H)$, anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{	ext{AHE}}$), magneto-infrared spectral features ($	ext{T}\alpha, 	ext{T} eta, 	ext{T}\gamma$), and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillation frequencies.
important_parameters: Exchange coupling strength ($J_{	ext{ex}}$) leading to $\sim 300	ext{ meV}$ band shifts; critical magnetic fields required for phase transitions (e.g., $1	ext{ T}$); temperature dependence near Néel temperatures ($\sim 4.5	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed electronic structure evolution and transport anomalies are directly governed by the strong, field-tunable exchange coupling mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures detail structural characterization (XRD), magnetic phase diagrams mapping transitions between AFM, $2/3$-FiMa, and FM states; magneto-IR spectra show evolving optical transitions correlated with magnetization; transport measurements map out angular dependence of AHE and $	ext{SdH}$ oscillations.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the magneto-topological phase diagram by first characterizing the magnetic ground state (AFM) via susceptibility and $M(H)$ curves. It then uses spectroscopy and transport to link field-induced magnetic transitions ($	ext{AFMa} ightarrow 2/3	ext{-FiMa} ightarrow 	ext{FMa}$) to specific topological electronic states, culminating in the demonstration of Weyl node tuning.
why_interesting: The strong coupling mechanism provides a clear pathway for using magnetism (a many-body phenomenon) to engineer and control exotic quantum band structures like Weyl semimetals, which is highly relevant for designing next-generation spintronic or topological electronic devices.
